sources.evidence: The Spring 2026 update is a January 2026 snapshot and separates fixed-line, fixed-wireless, satellite affordability and mobile prediction evidence.
sources.guard: Snapshot availability, decent-broadband counts and satellite affordability must not be interpreted as a retail order accepted for a target property.

sources.evidence: Ofcom publishes fixed coverage, fixed performance and mobile coverage as distinct products; postcode fixed-performance files ended after the July 2024 methodology change.
sources.guard: Coverage availability and active-line performance are different measures; local-authority performance must not be assigned to a postcode or premise.

sources.evidence: The checker displays operator-predicted fastest speeds and area availability, including partial availability where only some properties are covered.
sources.guard: A green or amber area result is not proof of property-level retail orderability, installation or achieved speed.

sources.evidence: The broadband USO is a legal right to request at least 10 Mbit/s down and 1 Mbit/s up; BT or KCOM checks existing service, public plans within 12 months and build cost.
sources.guard: USO eligibility is a request-and-assessment pathway, not current coverage, a completed build or provider-neutral retail availability.

sources.evidence: The collection distinguishes current gigabit connectivity, future commercial plans and BDUK intervention plans at UPRN level.
sources.guard: The collection is a current planning view and explicitly is not a complete history of voucher, Gigahub or Superfast delivery.

sources.evidence: The guide defines recognised-premises, country, postcode, lot and subsidy-control fields, including White, Grey/Black, Under Review and Unassessed.
sources.guard: Unassessed is not NO_DATA or unavailable; recognised-premises and subsidy status must retain their source snapshot and field semantics.

sources.evidence: The outcome classifies premises as White, Grey, Black or Under Review and notes differences can arise from capture date and supplier participation.
sources.guard: Published classification totals and aggregated maps cannot be copied to an individual UPRN without the matching release and point-in-time record.

sources.evidence: Supplier returns cover current and planned premises at UPRN level, with three-year plans, technology, funding and public-intervention dependencies evaluated.
sources.guard: A submitted supplier plan is confidential planning evidence and can be reclassified; it is not a public promise, activation date or accepted retail order.

sources.evidence: Public Review validates supplier evidence, Under Review premises are not White initial scope, and BDUK discourages postcode-only coverage returns.
sources.guard: Procurement eligibility and the line-in-the-sand process must not be treated as current commercial availability or a parcel-level service result.

sources.evidence: The July release is a 16 July management-information snapshot, covers initial contract scope and warns of ingestion lag and non-comparability with official statistics.
sources.guard: Contract-level built counts cannot establish a target UPRN's live service or whether a contractual milestone has been met.

sources.evidence: The endpoint requires a valid UPRN, supports DPA/LPI datasets, logical/classification filters and multiple output CRSs, and returns epoch and last-update metadata.
sources.guard: A successful UPRN address response proves identifier lookup only; dataset, lifecycle filters, CRS and epoch must be retained before spatial use.

sources.evidence: OS Places separates Find, Postcode and UPRN capture/verification requests from Nearest, BBOX, Radius and Polygon geosearch requests.
sources.guard: A proximity or polygon search is not equivalent to an exact address or UPRN verification and must not create a parcel binding.

sources.evidence: DPA is matched to Royal Mail PAF and is not present for every property; LPI can represent non-postal objects and multiple identifiers around a BLPU, with parent UPRN and lifecycle fields.
sources.guard: Absence of DPA is not absence of a property; DPA/LPI multiplicity, parent-child relationships and non-postal objects must be handled explicitly.

sources.evidence: OS defines approved, provisional and historic logical states; under-construction, in-use and no-longer-existing BLPU states; RPC positional accuracy and match-score bands.
sources.guard: Historic, provisional, low-accuracy or partial-match records must not be silently treated as a current exact address or parcel match.

sources.evidence: The BBOX endpoint returns address records within a supplied bounding box and supports lifecycle, classification and country filters.
sources.guard: Bounding-box inclusion is a spatial candidate operation; it does not prove that an address point lies in a legal title or target parcel.

sources.evidence: The Polygon endpoint accepts authenticated GeoJSON polygon or multipolygon geometry and returns matching address records with filters.
sources.guard: Query geometry provenance, CRS and boundary meaning must be verified; returned addresses do not establish title ownership or broadband availability.

sources.evidence: FindMyAddress includes live and provisional properties and alternative addresses, excludes historical records from normal search, and imposes a daily personal-use search limit.
sources.guard: Public search absence is not authoritative NO_DATA; historical and high-volume requirements belong to licensed AddressBase products.

sources.evidence: The UPRN lifecycle covers planning to demolition; subdivisions create child UPRNs, demolished or merged properties become historic and identifiers are not reused.
sources.guard: Parent, child, historic and replacement UPRNs must remain distinct; coordinates or address similarity cannot transfer broadband evidence between them.

sources.evidence: INSPIRE contains indicative freehold registered-property polygons, can duplicate polygons across local-authority files and links each polygon ID to a title.
sources.guard: INSPIRE excludes leasehold and other tenures, one title can have several polygons, and exact title extent requires the individual title plan.

sources.evidence: HMLR geometry is captured in British National Grid and reprojection to web-map CRSs may shift features by up to 15 metres.
sources.guard: Reprojected polygons and address points require original CRS and transformation metadata; proximity after reprojection cannot establish a parcel binding.

sources.evidence: The National Polygon Dataset carries polygon ID, title number, insert/update dates, version and record status, and documents gaps, slivers, underlaps and inconsistent extents.
sources.guard: Polygon versions and record status must be retained; index polygons are an index and can be larger or smaller than the title-plan extent.

sources.evidence: Most registered titles use general boundaries; exact legal boundaries are rarely shown and determined boundaries require a separate process.
sources.guard: A title-plan line, INSPIRE polygon or OS feature must not be described as the exact legal boundary unless determined-boundary evidence is present.
